description.summary: Loong OS app integration with the system shell

protocol.description:
Private protocol between Loong OS apps and the system shell (loong-shell). It lets an app describe how the system UI drawn on top of it should look. In version 1 this is the status bar: the time, Wi-Fi and battery that loong-shell draws over the top 24 logical pixels of every fullscreen app.
The status bar has two inks: ink (dark glyphs, for light backgrounds) and moon-white (light glyphs, for dark backgrounds). For the app in front, loong-shell picks the ink in this order:
1. the style set with loong_app_surface_v1.set_status_bar_style, unless it is "auto"; 2. the theme colour set with loong_app_surface_v1.set_theme_color: the ink with the higher WCAG 2.x contrast ratio against that colour; 3. sampling the pixels under the status bar (only for wl_shm and single-pixel buffers; GPU buffers are never read back); 4. the system appearance (light or dark).
The lock screen, the home screen and the app switcher always follow the system appearance. Changes of ink are cross-faded by the shell, so the state in this protocol is applied immediately (it is not double-buffered on wl_surface.commit): a client does not have to commit its surface for a change to take effect, which matters for clients whose surface commits are driven by a toolkit (WebKit).
The global is only advertised by loong-shell. Clients must treat it as optional and keep working without it.
Warning! This protocol is private to Loong OS and may change without notice. Backward compatible changes are added together with a version bump of the interfaces; incompatible changes get a new interface name.

interface.name: loong_app_manager_v1
interface.description: A global used to attach Loong OS app state to the surfaces of an app.

entry.name: already_constructed
entry.summary: the surface already has a loong_app_surface_v1 object

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. Objects created through it are not affected.

request.name: get_app_surface

description.summary: extend a surface with Loong OS app state

request.description:
Create a loong_app_surface_v1 object for the given surface.
The surface should be the root wl_surface of an xdg_toplevel (the surface that has the xdg_surface role, not one of its subsurfaces). Objects created for other surfaces are accepted, but their state is ignored in version 1.
If the surface already has a loong_app_surface_v1 object, the already_constructed protocol error is raised.

interface.name: loong_app_surface_v1

description.summary: Loong OS app state of a surface

interface.description:
Describes how the system UI on top of an app window should be drawn.
All state starts unset ("auto", no theme colour) and is applied as soon as the request is received (see the protocol description). If the wl_surface is destroyed first, this object becomes inert: its requests are ignored and it should be destroyed.

entry.name: invalid_style
entry.summary: set_status_bar_style was given an unknown style

enum.name: status_bar_style

description.summary: ink of the status bar glyphs

enum.description: Named after the colour of the status bar content, like UIStatusBarStyle: "dark_content" means dark glyphs.

entry.name: auto
entry.summary: let the shell decide (theme colour, sampling, system appearance)

entry.name: dark_content
entry.summary: ink (dark) glyphs, for apps whose top area is light

entry.name: light_content
entry.summary: moon-white (light) glyphs, for apps whose top area is dark

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the object. The status bar style goes back to "auto" and the theme colour is unset.

request.name: set_status_bar_style
request.description:
Set the ink of the status bar while this app is in front. "auto" (the initial value) lets the shell decide from the theme colour, from sampling the window, and finally from the system appearance.
Apps whose top area always matches the system appearance do not need this request. Apps that draw their own light or dark top area independently of the system appearance (a browser toolbar, a photo viewer, a video player) should set it.
An unknown style raises the invalid_style protocol error.

request.name: set_theme_color

description.summary: colour of the top area of the app

request.description:
Set the colour of the area of the app behind the status bar (the top 24 logical pixels), for example the theme colour of a web page (meta name="theme-color" or the theme_color of its manifest).
The colour is 0xAARRGGBB, not premultiplied. A value with zero alpha (in particular 0) unsets the theme colour. A translucent colour is composited over the paper colour of the system appearance before the shell compares contrast ratios.
The theme colour is only used while the status bar style is "auto".
